page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-4-lssd is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor operating at 2.3 GHz. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The memory configuration consists of 31.0 GB of RAM, providing a resource density of 7.75 GB per core. For local storage, the instance includes a bundled 137 GB NVMe SSD, while no GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provided.

The underlying Intel Xeon processor is equipped with an extensive L3 cache of 504 MB, alongside 2 MB L2 and 48 KB L1d caches. It supports advanced instruction sets, including Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX, AVX-512) and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and int8 operations. Cryptographic acceleration is supported via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI flags, alongside virtualization capabilities through VMX.

Performance benchmarks indicate a contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is generally average, as demonstrated by stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores, with a notable top-tier result in Geekbench text processing and strong performance in single-threaded gzip compression. However, multi-core CPU performance, software compilation, and memory bandwidth tests fall into the weak to poor categories. Large block memory read bandwidth is particularly limited, registering at 22.46 GB/sec.

Given the high memory-to-vCPU ratio and the inclusion of a fast local NVMe SSD, this server offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. It is suited for text processing, single-threaded compression tasks, Redis caching, and light database operations. However, the weak multi-core scaling and low memory bandwidth make it less suitable for heavy multi-threaded compilation, complex physics simulations, or large-scale LLM text generation.
